parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs functioning courts and partial protections with documented, traveller-facing hostile rules. Entry officers are instructed to refuse on document discrepancy and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; X/mismatched passports are barred nationally and upheld by the Supreme Court. Facility bans cover many jurisdictions, with criminal trespass in four and a documented handcuffed restroom arrest and 24-hour men's-ward hold. Custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse, and prison policy mandates hormone removal. Courts have enjoined some orders and employment/hate-crime protection remains, so imprisonment for being trans is not routine and execution is not credible, but outing can trigger refusal, detention, misgendered custody and care denial.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport X/mismatched markers barred, Supreme Court allowed it; entry cable directs refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; civil-liberties suit pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud allegation, detention and custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse reported; prisons mandate hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; restroom arrestee held in men's ward 24h.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts enjoin some orders and hear suits; bail/pretrial release occurred; no documented execution for trans status.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facility use or document issue can lead to birth-sex custody placement and documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 9 jurisdictions ban identity-consistent facilities in all government buildings, 9 cover schools plus some government buildings, 3 schools-only; 4 make use criminal in circumstances, trespass on refusal to leave.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 jurisdictions plus capital district have no mapped ban; statute requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, with exemptions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National binary-sex order reinforces state bans; traveller exposure depends sharply on jurisdiction visited.

care_services.exposure: Adult gender-affirming surgery cancelled at coastal hospital citing federal/state law; minors' care banned in division and 27 jurisdictions; proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18.
care_services.protection: Public-employee plan settlement requires payment for medically necessary care, possibly outside jurisdiction for minors.
care_services.interaction: Funding denial and state ban interact to contract adult and minor care despite settlement payment route.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders redefine sex as binary at birth, target gender ideology, direct investigations/prosecution over social transition of minors, military and sports bans, counterterrorism language about radically pro-transgender groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Employment discrimination barred under 2020 ruling, gender-identity hate crimes punishable nationally, marriage recognized, several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing coexists with court blocks; law-enforcement discretion and litigation status determine current effect.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans hormone/surgery under 18 with licence revocation; federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; hospitals subpoenaed for minor records; school facility bans.
minors_guardians.protection: Pre-July 2023 hormone continuation allowed; health-plan settlement may pay for out-of-state minor care; guardians can seek care elsewhere.
minors_guardians.interaction: Parent seeking care or school enrolment for minor faces ban, funding and investigation exposure distinct from adult visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police investigated three 2023 violent crimes against trans women in major city, described as epidemic-level; no denominator or outcome documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally; 22 jurisdictions plus capital district ban gender-identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence rate figure is an acknowledged undercount floor, so not used as elevated prevalence; police response outcome not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are slow, jurisdiction-dependent, and oversight has not prevented custody or facility practices; data on current enforceability of division care ban and hospital suspension permanence not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, legal-aid FAQ, injunctions, ombudsman-type suits and compensation avenues exist and sometimes succeed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working courts mitigate some federal orders but do not cancel enforced entry, facility or custody rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in passport/phone confiscation, prolonged questioning and fines without effective complaint redress, but here courts sometimes enjoin orders and some jurisdictions have no facility ban, so higher than 0.35.

Similar administrative refusal and secondary screening at entry, but here refusal can trigger fraud/lifetime ineligibility consideration, criminal trespass arrest, and documented custody abuse, so lower than 0.55.

Unlike 0.75-C where mismatched passports lead to brief detention, counsel and compensation, here markers are barred by policy upheld by the highest court and facility use can be criminal, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: binary document rules at entry, state facility bans and possible trespass arrest, birth-sex custody if detained, and contracted care. Courts, injunctions, hate-crime and employment law, and no-ban jurisdictions prevent a 0.35 rating, but they do not neutralize enforced hostile rules. Execution is not documented as credible and imprisonment for trans status is not routine, placing the case near 0.45-0.55 anchors, below pure administrative friction and above routine detention with no remedy.
